Package dev.px.core.concurrent

Class ThreadService

java.lang.Object
dev.px.core.concurrent.ThreadService
All Implemented Interfaces:
Named, Service
public final class ThreadService extends Object implements Service
The client's background thread pool.

Everything off the game thread goes through here so shutdown has a single place to wait on, and so a stray task cannot keep the JVM alive: the threads are daemons and named, which also makes them identifiable in a profiler or a crash report.

A task that throws is logged rather than vanishing. A raw ExecutorService swallows exceptions into the Future nobody checks, which is how background failures go unnoticed for weeks.

    • start

      public void start()
      Description copied from interface: Service
      Brings the service up. Throwing aborts startup with the service named, which is the right outcome for a broken subsystem: a half-started client is worse than one that says which piece failed.

    • repeat

      public ScheduledFuture<?> repeat(Runnable task, long initialDelay, long period, TimeUnit unit)
      Runs task repeatedly.

      Uses fixed-delay rather than fixed-rate scheduling: if one run overruns the period, fixed-rate fires the backlog all at once, which is exactly the wrong behaviour for polling a web API or a file.
